reads_as: a calm guy on a laptop bridging 'ZERO' to 'SOFTWARE ENGINEER' via a bold yellow arrow in 4 months
layout_map: Warm interior photo, man center-frame seated on a bed working a MacBook (Apple-logo glowing red) lower-right. Headline split across the top: 'ZERO' in yellow Anton-style caps on a black highlight box, top-left cells 1-2 (~x40-300, y30-110); a thick yellow right-arrow points from it across the man's head (~x340-510, y50-95); 'SOFTWARE / ENGINEER' yellow caps on black box, top-right two lines cells 6-8 (~x540-940, y30-180). A skewed yellow ribbon '4 MONTHS!' in black caps sits mid-left over his shoulder (~x30-380, y250-340, rotated ~-8deg). Face centered ~x430,y220, head-and-shoulders crop, ~30% frame coverage. Accent yellow.
why_it_works: the arrow literally draws the zero-to-hero transformation while the casual posture says 'this was achievable for an ordinary person'
mimic_for: a learning-journey or transformation explainer that promises a fast path from a beginner state to a senior outcome
title: How I Learned to Code in 4 MONTHS & Got a Job Offer (no CS Degree)

reads_as: a laptop running real Python code flanked by a Python logo and output icons under a bold 'POWER OF PYTHON' banner
layout_map: Soft desaturated desk/office background. Headline banner across the very top, full width cells 1-8 (y30-130): 'POWER OF' black caps on yellow highlight blocks, with 'OF' inverted (yellow caps on a black block) in the middle for rhythm, then 'PYTHON' black on yellow at right. A floating MacBook centered (~x430-850, y150-620) showing a real VS Code editor with photoEditor.py source. Large blue-and-yellow Python logo floats left of the laptop (~x90-310, y230-470). Three rounded output-app icons (image stack, file-copy, red YouTube play) stacked right (~x1050-1200, y180-560), each linked to the laptop by a dotted connector line. No face. Accent yellow with Python blue/yellow.
why_it_works: showing actual code plus the language logo and concrete outputs promises a real buildable project, not abstract theory
mimic_for: a hands-on coding tutorial or project video where the payoff is real source code producing tangible outputs
title: 3 PYTHON AUTOMATION PROJECTS FOR BEGINNERS
